decisions.decision: The Constitution has absolute normative authority.
The Constitution applies to the entire project.
GitHub protection applies to policy files and code alike.
ECMAScript 2015 is the baseline; newer features require proof.
Execution contexts are explicitly separated.
Official documentation defines the documented contract; reproducible tests establish observed behavior.
TypeScript and ESLint are supporting checks, not sources of truth; no DOM or Node globals in the main runtime; target and lib remain separate.
External libraries are denied by default until reviewed.
Layered verification and automated gates block on failure.
High-risk operations are blocked by default and require approved exceptions.
Unverified memory limits are not treated as official limits; measurements require evidence.
Components declare supported contexts explicitly.
Documented, Tested, Compatible, Incompatible, and Not Verified are distinct assessment dimensions.
Source hierarchy is explicit, with Scriptable official documentation first.
GitHub Actions is the mandatory CI gate, separate from device testing.
Exceptions require approval and documented scope, reason, risk, and controls.
Architecture uses Core, Data, Services, Features, and UI layers with Scriptable Host APIs.
A central compatibility register records each API or feature assessment.
Minimum Scriptable and iOS versions are evidence-based, not guessed.
The device matrix includes iPhone and iPad and records differences.
New, changed, uncertain, or risky APIs require Scriptable Runtime proof.
Backward compatibility and deprecation require reason, affected users, alternative, transition period, and records.
Breaking changes include incompatible changes to scripts, API contracts, outputs, side effects, or runtime requirements.
Enforcement uses BLOCK, WARN, and GUIDE.
Author, reviewer, exception approver, register steward, and policy owner responsibilities are distinct, though one person may hold multiple roles.
A central evidence register records evidence identifiers and metadata.
Normative language uses MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY.
Each rule has an ID, title, statement, scope, severity, rationale, source, verification, exception conditions, and owner.
Explicit precedence prevents lower-level rules from overriding higher-level rules.
Rules apply across scripts, modules, libraries, dependencies, settings, tests, tools, CI, and documentation, with applicability declared.
Evidence is valid only for its tested scope and must be rechecked after material changes.
Exception lifecycle is Proposed, Reviewed, Approved, Active, Expired or Revoked.
The Constitution uses Semantic Versioning with Major, Minor, and Patch changes.
A compatibility proof unit is a component/API/version/device/context/result/evidence tuple.
Script, Module, Library, and Dependency are distinct concepts.
Runtime, Execution Context, and Host API are distinct concepts.
Compatibility assessment dimensions are independent, not mutually exclusive states.
Incompatible, Not Verified, and Unsupported are distinct.
Reference sources and proof sources are distinct.
Policy Rule, Scope, Enforcement, Exception, Evidence, and Decision have explicit relationships.
Each API/version/device/context combination has its own compatibility record.
Evidence classes are explicitly categorized.
Runtime test evidence includes reproduction steps, inputs, expected and actual results, and environment.
Conflicting evidence is retained and analyzed, not deleted.
Evidence is classified as valid for scope, requiring re-verification, or superseded.
Risk uses impact, likelihood, and detection difficulty.
Compatible requires sufficient, current evidence for the declared scope.
Unknown supported versions are recorded as Pending Verification, not guessed.
Device targets are listed and distinguished from tested devices.
Role responsibilities are defined even if a person holds several roles.
Evidence review is event- and risk-driven, not based on one universal expiry period.
Risk considers likelihood, impact severity, and difficulty of detection.
Every exception has an expiry date.
Violation handling follows a recorded detect, classify, assign, remediate or request exception, verify, and close workflow.
CI reruns relevant checks after dependency, tool, or governance changes and does not claim device proof.
Unverified versions remain Not Verified until evidence exists.
Device support is declared only with matrix coverage and evidence.
Role names are defined first; personal assignments require verified authority.
Exception renewal requires a new review and approval.
Evidence review is triggered by material changes and risk.
One structured canonical source holds compatibility records.
CI success cannot replace physical-device or context-specific tests.
Documents are layered into Constitution, Policies, Standards/Procedures, Records, and References.
English is used for normative terms and technical fields, with Arabic explanation where useful.
Rule IDs remain stable and are never reused.
Every rule traces to scope, enforcement, checks, evidence, exceptions, and decisions.
Constitutional changes follow proposal, impact, review, approval, release, and synchronization.
Rules have Proposed, Active, Deprecated, and Retired lifecycle states.
Human documents and structured canonical data are separated and linked.
A constitutional release requires version classification, record integrity, CI, approval, and date.
Rule conflicts are recorded and resolved by precedence.
Wide-impact changes require documented impact analysis.
Historical and conflicting evidence is retained.
Failed or untrustworthy enforcement tools produce BLOCKED or INDETERMINATE, not success.
Dependency review includes source, version, integrity, transitive dependencies, security, and license.
A bad release is corrected through a later release with traceable rollback impact, not erased history.
Drift between documentation, rules, tests, and actual behavior is recorded and remediated.
The Constitution is reviewed after major platform, architecture, dependency, or threat-model changes.
